authorization: The user asked whether C=2 is genuinely slower overall and whether B550's topology can reduce the penalty; prior standing authorization covers bounded stops of the embedding replicas for Strata measurements.
scope: Measure focused C=2 topology alternatives for the pinned Qwen IQ2_XS/Q2_0 MTP serving path, including batch-group choices, split placement, independent per-GPU servers, a shared CPU expert arena, and serial queueing on the two-GPU solo path.

question_answer.is_c2_slower_overall: Yes for the built-in batch path. The topology-aware default (auto K=24, --batch-groups auto) fell from 142.66 aggregate tok/s at C=1 to 127.02 at C=2, a 10.95 percent aggregate loss. Per-request decode median fell from 176.6 to 75.65 tok/s.
question_answer.best_builtin_c2: Auto K=24 with --batch-groups auto. One shared group, split-30 grouping, and per-GPU process sharding were all slower.
question_answer.better_topology_aware_fallback: For exactly two short requests, do not use batch slots: keep the split-30 two-GPU solo/MTP path and queue the requests serially. An exact binary-search prompt pair completed ten requests at 222.53 aggregate tok/s with 252.6 tok/s median per-request decode. First-request wall was about 0.42-0.44 s and second-request wall about 0.83-0.88 s.
question_answer.comparison_caveat: The 222.53 figure uses the exact repeated binary-search prompt and 94-token completions. The varied-prompt driver measured split-30 solo/serial-class C=1 at 137.49 aggregate tok/s against 106.29 for split-30 C=2 batch slots. The direction is consistent under both workload styles, but 222.53 is not a same-prompt-family comparison to 127.02.

exact_prompt_pair_alternatives.memory: about 71 GiB RAM used and 2.4 GiB swap

exact_prompt_pair_alternatives.shared_arena: 33 GiB in /dev/shm, pack hash checked, cudaHostRegister PORTABLE ok in both processes

exact_prompt_pair_alternatives.arm: serial queue on two-GPU split-30 solo/MTP path

serial_queue_walls_seconds.note: One pair swapped queue order; the observed walls still show one request near 0.42 s and the other near 0.83 s. Ten exact-prompt requests completed in 4.224 s total.

interpretation.builtin_batch_penalty: The topology-aware two-group pipeline is already the best built-in C=2 mode. It cannot preserve the solo MTP path: batch-slot requests lose the solo draft behavior/reporting and each verify window carries one token per conversation, so per-request decode falls even though both cards remain busy.
interpretation.why_process_sharding_does_not_help: One full model per card leaves only about 13.7k of 24.6k experts resident per GPU and competes for CPU/RAM. Sharing the 32.23 GiB CPU arena removes duplication but does not improve throughput (104.79 versus 109.11 tok/s), so the bottleneck is not merely duplicate RAM.
interpretation.recommendation: Use split-30 two-GPU serial queueing for an agent fallback tier at concurrency <=2, especially short tool calls. Enable batch slots only when fairness across more than two longer concurrent conversations matters more than total latency. A future engine optimization would need topology-aware batch MTP across a layer split; current --batch-mtp is explicitly one-GPU-only.

credentials_and_host_incident.hf_token_refresh: The valid Mac token was copied to B550 and Strix with mode 0600. hf auth whoami reports user Kearm on both. The B550 hf-anon-trust.conf drop-in was removed, daemon-reloaded, and both embedding units restarted successfully; :1238 returned a 1536-dim embedding. Strix's standalone embedder was also restarted without the anonymous workaround and returned a 1536-dim embedding.
credentials_and_host_incident.network_incident: During the shared-arena run, B550's Realtek enp7s0 link dropped for 52 seconds and returned; journalctl shows r8169 Link Down at 18:10:53 and Link Up at 18:11:45, with no OOM, GPU reset, or panic. The run had already completed, the restore trap removed the shared file, and both embedding units were active afterward. A later brief SSH disconnect also recovered without a new kernel Link Down line in the queried five-minute window.
credentials_and_host_incident.non_cause_claim: The shared-arena configuration was running when the first link flap occurred, but the kernel log attributes the outage to enp7s0 link state; this record does not claim the GPU or shared-memory experiment caused it.

non_claims: The exact-prompt serial result is not a same-workload substitute for the varied-prompt 127.02 tok/s batch number; both are reported and the comparison caveat is explicit.
Five rounds per arm and one exact-prompt paired control are short-prompt observations, not a broad agent workload matrix.
Queueing is recommended for concurrency <=2 and short requests; it is not shown superior for long generations, prompts much larger than 25 tokens, or more than two clients.
Batch-slot MTP behavior remains unconfirmed because batch timings do not populate draft counters; process-shard and serial controls did report active drafts.
No deployed Strata configuration or routing tier was changed.
The Realtek link flap is recorded as an operational hazard, not diagnosed or repaired.
